prior_exposure: The registered question and earlier report disclose that a two-reader ar/ar sequence is being compared with the ZL aram-tail reading. This is not a blind semantic test.

scope.target: already admitted f85r2.24 inner written annulus

whole_line_observation.layout: A narrow annular writing track encircles the blue central disk and figure. The fixed rotations show the complete ring and its breaks; the requested locus is in this ring, not the large outer text blocks.
whole_line_observation.ink_and_stroke: Small brown ink with variable darkness and fine strokes. Some marks merge optically where strokes touch or nearly touch; pale gaps are brief and not consistently wide.
whole_line_observation.coverage: The full visible annular line was viewed in the whole central crop orientations. I can inventory the continuous stroke track, but not assign a fully certain token boundary to every faint cluster from these permitted renditions.

segments_and_gaps.position: upper arc, immediately clockwise from the upper-left break
segments_and_gaps.observation: Several short, angular clusters follow the curved band. At least two pale interruptions separate darker strokes; one interruption could be a narrow word gap or a break between components within a group.
segments_and_gaps.certainty: moderate for separate ink clusters; low for orthographic grouping

segments_and_gaps.observation: A short run of compact strokes with small curved/open forms and adjacent upright or hooked marks. One darker patch is continuous at this scale; its internal strokes are not cleanly separable.
The writing remains on the same curved track. There are visible light gaps between some clusters, but the script leans with the arc, so apparent gaps vary with orientation and pen fade.
segments_and_gaps.certainty: moderate for track continuity; low for every group boundary

segments_and_gaps.position: lower-right terminal area shown in the fixed 2x tail view
segments_and_gaps.observation: Two neighboring compact clusters have broadly similar rounded/open marks followed or accompanied by short angular strokes. A thin pale interval is visible between their darker cores in the best rotation. A small set of strokes extending after the second dark core is visible, but the allowed view does not settle whether these strokes belong to that same cluster or begin a distinct final cluster.
segments_and_gaps.certainty: moderate that two dark clusters are physically distinguishable; low on the final boundary and exact stroke membership

segments_and_gaps.observation: A sequence of small groups continues around the band; several strokes are lighter than the central dark forms, and at least one apparent gap is partly obscured by the adjacent blue coloring and ring contour.
segments_and_gaps.certainty: moderate for visible groups; low for faint strokes and spacing

segments_and_gaps.observation: The line curves back to its upper starting region. Short dark groups remain visible; faint marks near the break do not show a decisive terminal punctuation or a uniquely identifiable line end.
segments_and_gaps.certainty: moderate for line continuation; low for the exact closure point

specific_disputed_stroke_account.first_cluster: A compact rounded/open stroke form with a nearby short angular stroke; exact glyph identity uncertain.
specific_disputed_stroke_account.second_cluster: A broadly similar rounded/open core with additional short strokes; exact glyph identity uncertain.
specific_disputed_stroke_account.separation: A narrow visible pale interval separates the two darker cores in the r270/tail views, so two clusters are a plausible segmentation. It is not a large, unambiguous gap.
specific_disputed_stroke_account.possible_trailing_marks: A further small rightward/curved sequence is present after the second core. Whether it is attached to that group, a third group, or a flourish is unresolved.
specific_disputed_stroke_account.why_zl_tail_still_open: The crucial distinction is attachment of the small post-core strokes and whether the inter-core interval is a full word space. Stroke visibility supports a local two-cluster reading more than a single uninterrupted dark blob, but does not resolve the full terminal segmentation.

limits: No glyph string, Latin-letter transcription, meaning, or reader preference is assigned.
No alias, normalization, majority reading, or new canonical character is proposed.
A two-cluster visual impression cannot establish the characters ar, the suffix am, or any type consequence.
The comparison concerns one manuscript image and an informed observer; it is not independent confirmation.
